description: We are Team AstraNova a passionate group of students participating in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. Our challenge is to build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer that makes space exploration exciting and educational. We are interested in coding AI software development web technologies and space scienceWe aim to develop an innovative interactive and user-friendly solution through teamwork creativityand problemsolving. We welcome enthusiastic members who love technology and space exploration!
summary:
AstroVault – NASA Space Hardware Explorer is an educational website developed by Team AstraNova for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It focuses on NASA hardware left across the Solar System, including equipment on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space. The project introduces school-age students to the stories, purposes, and status of space missions. 
AstroVault explains space hardware through language and a child-friendly interface. It features the Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP), Lunar Roving Vehicle, Sojourner rover, Spirit and Opportunity rovers, and Voyager 1 and 2. The website groups these explorers by location and mission, helping users understand what each machine was designed to do, where it travelled, and why it mattered. Interactive elements include a 3D gallery and quizzes that make learning enjoyable.

The project addresses the challenge by turning technical mission information into accessible stories for space enthusiasts. Rather than presenting only dates and facts, AstroVault helps students connect with the discoveries and engineering achievements behind space exploration. It is important because these machines represent human curiosity, innovation, and perseverance. By preserving their stories in an interactive platform, AstroVault can inspire students to explore science, technology, engineering, and space research, while appreciating the legacy of NASA missions.
details:
AstroVault – NASA Space Hardware Explorer is an educational web platform designed to introduce school-age students to NASA's space hardware left across the Solar System, including the Moon, Mars, and deep space.

The platform explains different space exploration technologies, their original purposes, current operational status, and the scientific discoveries they helped achieve. Information is organized by location and mission so that students can easily understand the history and importance of each piece of hardware. Interactive learning elements, including quizzes and a visual gallery, are planned to make the experience more engaging.

The main benefit of AstroVault is that it transforms complex space mission information into simple, accessible, and interesting educational content. Its intended impact is to increase students' curiosity about space exploration and inspire interest in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM).

The project is being developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the website's structure, design, and interactive functionality. NASA's publicly available mission information and images are intended as reference materials. GitHub and GitHub Pages are used for project development and web hosting.

The creative aspect of AstroVault is its approach of telling the stories of space hardware rather than simply listing technical information. The team considers educational value, scientific accuracy, accessibility, user-friendly design, and engagement for young learners.

Our goal is to preserve the legacy of NASA's space exploration missions and help the next generation understand the technology and discoveries that continue to shape our understanding of the universe.
